annotations.description: In Limited formats, choosing to be on the play is almost always correct. Being on the play gives you tempo advantage — you get to play lands and threats first, which is critical in Limited where board presence matters most. Choosing to draw (letting the opponent go first) gives you an extra card but sacrifices the tempo advantage, which is generally not worth it unless you have a very specific control deck that wants the extra card.
annotations.actionTaken: Chose to be on the draw (selected opponent as starting player)
annotations.betterLine: Choose to be on the play (select yourself as starting player) to gain tempo advantage, which is the default correct choice in Limited.

annotations.description: Mulliganed a strong 7-card hand that had 3 lands, a powerful curve (Turn 2 Hero's Blade, Turn 4 Balan auto-equipping for a 6/5 first strike), and a backup plan with Soulcage Fiend and Kothophed. The only weakness was having just 1 Swamp for BB costs, but the primary game plan (Hero's Blade + Balan) only needs Plains.
annotations.actionTaken: Chose to mulligan to 6 cards
annotations.betterLine: Keep the 7-card hand. Hero's Blade into Balan is an extremely strong synergy that's castable with the available mana, and 3 lands is a fine starting count.

annotations.description: Bottomed the only Swamp (black mana source) instead of a redundant Plains. The hand has 3 Plains which already covers the white mana costs for all spells in hand (Honor Guard, Chains of Custody, Kwende). The 4th land (Swamp) provides crucial access to the deck's second color for any black spells drawn later.
annotations.actionTaken: Bottomed the Swamp, leaving hand with 3 Plains and no black mana source
annotations.betterLine: Bottom a Plains instead, keeping 2 Plains + 1 Swamp (or even 3 Plains + 1 Swamp if keeping 4 lands). This maintains access to black mana while still curving out perfectly with the white spells in hand.

annotations.description: Playing Swamp instead of Thriving Isle on turn 2. Thriving Isle enters tapped, and with only 2 mana available this turn, there's nothing to cast anyway. Playing the tapped land now means it's untapped on turn 3 for a 3-drop (Wavebreak Hippocamp, Infernal Idol, or even Vendilion Clique with flash). Playing Swamp now forces Thriving Isle to come in tapped on turn 3, losing a full turn of tempo on 3-drops.
annotations.actionTaken: Played Swamp (untapped land) on turn 2 with no 2-mana plays available.
annotations.betterLine: Play Thriving Isle (choosing black) on turn 2 so it enters tapped now and is available untapped on turn 3, enabling a turn-3 three-drop.

annotations.description: Timed out on Thriving Isle color choice. The deck is UB with multiple black-heavy cards in hand (Skullslither Worm, Strangling Spores, Yargle). Black is clearly the correct choice to have a dual-color land producing both Blue and Black. The timeout likely defaulted to a useless color like White, making the Thriving Isle effectively a worse Island for the rest of the game.
annotations.actionTaken: Timed out, getting a default color choice (likely White) instead of actively choosing.
annotations.betterLine: Choose Black for Thriving Isle to have access to both Blue and Black mana, supporting the heavy black requirements in hand.

annotations.description: With no castable spells this turn (Chains of Custody has no valid target since opponent controls no nonland permanents, and Kwende costs 4), the extra untapped mana from Swamp is wasted. Thriving Moor entering tapped costs nothing this turn and provides better color flexibility (can choose white for an extra white source).
annotations.actionTaken: Played Swamp (untapped) when there were no 3-mana plays available this turn.
annotations.betterLine: Play Thriving Moor (choosing white) since it enters tapped at no cost when you have no plays, saving Swamp for a future turn when entering untapped matters.

annotations.description: Failed to attack with Benalish Honor Guard into an empty board with no blockers and no untapped mana on the opponent's side. This is 2 free damage that was left on the table.
annotations.actionTaken: Timed out and did not declare any attackers.
annotations.betterLine: Attack with Benalish Honor Guard for 2 unblockable damage against the empty board.

annotations.description: Cast Chains of Custody when the opponent has no nonland permanents on the battlefield, meaning the exile ETB trigger has no valid target and does nothing. This wastes one of the best white removal spells in limited just to give a 2/2 ward {2}.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Chains of Custody on Benalish Honor Guard with no opponent nonland permanents to exile
annotations.betterLine: Hold Chains of Custody for when the opponent plays actual threats to exile. Could pass the turn and save it for a meaningful target later.

annotations.description: Declined to cast Fleeting Distraction as a cantrip when there was a legal target (Benalish Honor Guard) and no other meaningful use for the mana this turn. With 2 available mana and nothing else castable, drawing a card for U would have been free value to help dig toward lands and playable spells.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority without casting Fleeting Distraction
annotations.betterLine: Cast Fleeting Distraction targeting Benalish Honor Guard to draw a card, since there's no better use for the U mana this turn and the hand needs to find land drops to deploy expensive threats like Yargle and Skullslither Worm.

annotations.description: Playing Thriving Moor (which enters tapped) instead of Plains or Swamp means only 3 mana is available this turn, delaying Kwende, Pride of Femeref by a full turn. Kwende is a powerful 2/2 double striker that also gives Benalish Honor Guard +1/+0 (legendary synergy), making it a 3/2. Getting Kwende down a turn earlier is significant tempo.
annotations.actionTaken: Played Thriving Moor (enters tapped), leaving only 3 mana available this turn.
annotations.betterLine: Play Plains (or Swamp) to have 4 mana available and immediately cast Kwende, Pride of Femeref this turn.

annotations.description: Declined to cast Fleeting Distraction when having 1 blue mana available and no other use for it this turn. With a hand full of expensive cards (4+ mana) and only 3 lands in play, drawing a card to potentially find a land was valuable. No meaningful spells could be cast with the remaining mana regardless.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority without casting Fleeting Distraction
annotations.betterLine: Cast Fleeting Distraction targeting Benalish Honor Guard to draw a card and dig toward lands. The U mana would otherwise go unused, and finding a 4th land is critical for deploying threats like Skullslither Worm next turn. Alternatively, saving it for the opponent's combat to reduce Honor Guard's damage by 1 while drawing is also reasonable, but the land-finding urgency favors casting now.

annotations.description: Failed to attack with Benalish Honor Guard (2/2) into an empty board. The opponent has no creatures, so this is 2 free damage with zero risk.
annotations.actionTaken: Timed out and did not declare attackers
annotations.betterLine: Attack with Benalish Honor Guard for 2 unblockable damage against an empty board.

annotations.description: Declined to cast Fleeting Distraction on the attacking Benalish Honor Guard. Fleeting Distraction would reduce 2 damage to 1 damage and draw a card, all for just {U}. This is essentially free value — save 1 life and cantrip. The only argument for holding it is to later trigger Wavebreak Hippocamp's draw ability on the opponent's turn, but Hippocamp isn't in play yet and the immediate guaranteed value of saving life while cantripping is better than speculative future synergy.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority, taking 2 damage from Benalish Honor Guard instead of 1
annotations.betterLine: Cast Fleeting Distraction targeting Benalish Honor Guard to save 1 life and draw a card for {U}

annotations.description: Cast Kwende before playing a land drop. Playing Plains or Swamp first (both enter untapped) would give 5 mana total, allowing Kwende to be cast with 1 mana remaining open, which is strictly better than using all 4 available mana on Kwende and then playing a land with nothing to spend it on.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Kwende, Pride of Femeref with all 4 available mana before making the land drop.
annotations.betterLine: Play Plains (or Swamp) first, then cast Kwende, Pride of Femeref, leaving 1 mana open for potential interaction or flexibility.

annotations.description: Playing Plains instead of Swamp when the only spell in hand is Infernal Idol, which has a {1}{B}{B} activated ability. Swamp would better support both casting the Idol (generic cost) and eventually activating it.
annotations.actionTaken: Played Plains as the land drop
annotations.betterLine: Play Swamp to have better access to {B}{B} for Infernal Idol's sacrifice ability (would have 2 Swamps + Thriving Moor for 3 black sources)

annotations.description: Failed to attack with Benalish Honor Guard (3/2) when the opponent had no untapped creatures to block (Wavebreak Hippocamp is summoning sick). This was 3 free damage with zero risk.
annotations.actionTaken: Timed out and did not declare any attackers.
annotations.betterLine: Attack with Benalish Honor Guard for 3 unblockable damage, bringing opponent from 16 to 13 life.

annotations.description: Kimi25 Valley declined to attack with Wavebreak Hippocamp into a board where the only possible blocker is Kwende (2/2, just entered). If opponent doesn't block, it's 2 free damage. If opponent blocks with Kwende, Kimi25 can use Fleeting Distraction to shrink Kwende to 1/2, win combat, draw a card, AND remove the dangerous double strike lord. Either outcome is favorable.
annotations.actionTaken: Did not attack with Wavebreak Hippocamp.
annotations.betterLine: Attack with Wavebreak Hippocamp. If Kwende blocks, use Fleeting Distraction to win combat and draw a card. If Kwende doesn't block, deal 2 damage for free.

annotations.description: Cast Infernal Idol before playing a land drop. Should always play the land first to maximize available mana after casting spells, as there's no reason to hold the land. Playing Swamp first would leave 3 mana open after casting Infernal Idol instead of 2.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Infernal Idol with land drop still unused
annotations.betterLine: Play Swamp first, then cast Infernal Idol, leaving 3 mana open instead of 2

annotations.description: MiMo Coach timed out and failed to declare any attackers when they had a dominant board position. Kwende (2/2 double strike) and Benalish Honor Guard (3/2) could attack into a single Wavebreak Hippocamp (2/2) with all opponent's lands tapped. Any block scenario results in the Hippocamp dying while MiMo Coach's creatures survive, dealing 3-7 damage to a 13-life opponent. Missing this attack wastes a massive combat step.
annotations.actionTaken: No response - failed to declare any attackers
annotations.betterLine: Attack with all. In every blocking scenario, Hippocamp dies (Kwende's first strike or Honor Guard's 3 power kills it) and MiMo Coach deals 3-7 damage while losing nothing. This pressures the opponent significantly at 13 life.

annotations.description: Took 7 damage (going from 13 to 6 life) by not blocking, when blocking Benalish Honor Guard with Wavebreak Hippocamp would have traded the Hippocamp for the Honor Guard and saved 3 life (going to 10 instead). At 6 life, Kimi25 Valley is in serious danger. While Wavebreak Hippocamp has ongoing value for drawing cards off instant-speed spells, the life total is too precarious to justify preserving it over a profitable trade.
annotations.actionTaken: Declined to block, taking 7 damage (3 from Honor Guard + 4 from Kwende's double strike) to drop to 6 life.
annotations.betterLine: Block Benalish Honor Guard with Wavebreak Hippocamp to trade 2/2 for the 3/2 Honor Guard, taking only 4 damage from Kwende (going to 9 life) while removing a threat.

annotations.description: With opponent's creatures all tapped, Kimi25 Valley should play Swamp and cast Yargle (9/3) to attack into the defenseless board for 9 damage, bringing opponent to 11. Strangling Spores could be saved for the opponent's turn to get a Wavebreak Hippocamp draw trigger. Instead, they used the removal spell precombat when there was no immediate threat (all opponent creatures tapped) and missed a huge attack opportunity.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Strangling Spores in precombat main phase when opponent's creatures were tapped
annotations.betterLine: Play Swamp, cast Yargle Glutton of Urborg (9/3) for 4B, attack for 9 damage into tapped-out board, save Strangling Spores for opponent's turn to trigger Wavebreak Hippocamp card draw

annotations.description: Chose to kill Benalish Honor Guard (3/2) with Strangling Spores instead of Kwende, Pride of Femeref (2/2 double strike). Kwende is the far more threatening creature - it has double strike itself (effectively 4 damage per attack), grants double strike to first strikers, and its legendary status gives Honor Guard +1/+0. Removing Kwende would both eliminate the bigger threat AND weaken Honor Guard to a vanilla 2/2.
annotations.actionTaken: Targeted Benalish Honor Guard with Strangling Spores
annotations.betterLine: Target Kwende, Pride of Femeref with Strangling Spores to remove the double strike threat and simultaneously weaken Honor Guard from 3/2 to 2/2

annotations.description: Opponent is at 6 life with no creatures on the battlefield. Kwende (double strike, 2/2 = 4 damage) plus Benalish Honor Guard (3/2 = 3 damage) deals exactly 7 damage, which is lethal. The player timed out and failed to attack, missing a guaranteed kill.
annotations.actionTaken: Timed out and did not declare any attackers, missing lethal damage.
annotations.betterLine: Attack with both Kwende, Pride of Femeref and Benalish Honor Guard for 7 total damage (4 + 3), killing the opponent at 6 life.
